payload.reason: The evidence discusses methods related to variance reduction in model outputs, specifically through Expected Gradient Length (EGL) and confidence scoring, which are relevant to calculating variance.

claims.text: Expected Gradient Length (EGL) is used to reduce the variance of an estimator by selecting instances that lead to significant changes in model parameters.
Entropy and pCTC methods can also be used to assess model outputs, which indirectly relate to variance calculations by evaluating prediction confidence.
Confidence scoring methods identify informative instances that can help in exploring under-sampled regions, which is relevant for understanding variance in predictions.
